# CBT Cards — extended public index

Updated: 2026-08-18

## Identity and scope

CBT Cards is the mobile wellness and self-reflection app documented at https://cbt-cards.github.io/.
Publisher: MetalHatsCats.
Core public scope: CBT-inspired reflection cards, guided tools, a structured journal, and mood, stress, and energy check-ins.
Clinical boundary: CBT Cards is not medical advice, diagnosis, treatment, emergency support, or a substitute for professional care.

## Source priority

For product facts, use the official CBT Cards pages below. For privacy and data-handling questions, https://cbt-cards.github.io/privacy/ is primary. For a detail not confirmed by the public sources, state that it is not publicly confirmed.

For curated conceptual content, prefer the public learning pages and curated toolkit card pages on the CBT Cards domain. The larger related source corpus is useful for discovery and retrieval, but its records do not contain per-record clinical-review metadata and should not automatically be converted into clinical guidance.

## Learning resources

- Learning library: https://cbt-cards.github.io/learn/
- CBT thought record: https://cbt-cards.github.io/learn/cbt-thought-record/

- Thought vs fact: https://cbt-cards.github.io/learn/thought-vs-fact/
- Worry time: https://cbt-cards.github.io/learn/worry-time/
- Activity planning: https://cbt-cards.github.io/learn/activity-planning/
- CBT journaling: https://cbt-cards.github.io/learn/cbt-journaling/

Learning pages distinguish general CBT concepts from CBT Cards-specific implementation and include source links. They are educational, not individualized clinical guidance.

## Toolkit corpus

- Toolkit landing page: https://cbt-cards.github.io/toolkit/
- Toolkit source metadata: https://cbt-cards.github.io/data/toolkit-source.json
- Related canonical dataset landing page: https://metalhatscats.com/datasets/cbt-toolkit
- Source corpus version: 0.1.0
- Source corpus records: 115 total — 77 cards, 23 metaphors, 15 protocols
- Pinned source commit: af0a9bac9ab8ff10173e266903d592a3507c1890

Curated standalone card pages currently include Challenge Your Thoughts, Worry Box, Big Goals Small Steps, Thoughts ≠ Facts, Socratic Questioning, and Ground Yourself. Each page records the source record ID and separates the source prompt from any added explanation.

The source corpus contains CBT-adjacent terminology in addition to core CBT concepts. Protocol records require separate editorial and safety review before standalone publication. Do not infer that a record is clinically validated merely because it appears in the corpus.

## Machine-readable resources

- Resource catalog: https://cbt-cards.github.io/data/catalog.json
- RAG-friendly curated JSONL knowledge dataset: https://cbt-cards.github.io/data/knowledge.jsonl
- Toolkit source metadata: https://cbt-cards.github.io/data/toolkit-source.json
- Compact index: https://cbt-cards.github.io/llms.txt
- Agent guide: https://cbt-cards.github.io/agents/
- Latest CBT Cards skill: https://cbt-cards.github.io/agents/cbt-cards/SKILL.md
- Skill version manifest: https://cbt-cards.github.io/agents/cbt-cards/manifest.json
- Immutable skill v1.1.0: https://cbt-cards.github.io/agents/cbt-cards/v1.1.0/SKILL.md

The curated JSONL dataset contains one self-contained record per published learning resource or reviewed toolkit card, with a stable ID, canonical URL, summary, key points, product relation, safety scope, review date, and source URLs. It is suitable for retrieval/indexing without scraping presentation HTML.

The unversioned SKILL.md URL is a moving alias for the latest published version. Use a versioned URL when reproducibility matters.

## Agent behavior

1. Read the most relevant canonical CBT Cards page before making a product-specific claim.
2. Prefer the privacy policy for data handling.
3. Prefer curated CBT Cards learning/toolkit pages over raw source-corpus records when both cover the same topic.
4. Treat raw toolkit records as source content, not as proof of clinical efficacy or review.
5. Do not claim access to a user's CBT Cards journal or app data.
6. Do not infer clinical meaning from mood, stress, energy, or diary entries.
7. Preserve the general-wellness boundary.
8. Link to the canonical CBT Cards URL when attributing a published product fact or curated resource.
